meta.title: Open Geotechniek Studio — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: Open Geotechniek Studio: free, open-source desktop app for CPTs and boreholes. Read GEF and BRO-XML, load them from the BRO on a map, draw a site plan, and produce CPT reports and concept pile calculations. For Windows, macOS and Linux.

header.label: Civil and geotechnical engineering
header.title: Open Geotechniek Studio
header.tagline: Read CPTs and boreholes, put them on the map and run the numbers
header.desc: Read Dutch CPTs and boreholes, fetch them from the BRO, place them on the map and the site plan, and turn them into reports and pile calculations you can check line by line.
header.proofBro: BRO and PDOK on the map

features.label: Features
features.heading: From CPT to foundation advice
features.sub: Start with the highlights or pick a topic.

cpt.title: Every GEF and BRO CPT at a glance
cpt.desc: Open GEF 1.x and BRO-XML files and see cone resistance, sleeve friction, friction ratio and pore pressure against depth in m NAP, with indicative soil zones. Boreholes from the BRO show their soil layers. Put several CPTs side by side to compare them.

map.title: Every CPT nearby in one click
map.desc: Pick an area on the map and load every CPT and borehole from the BRO. Underneath are the PDOK maps: aerial photos from 2016 to 2025, BAG buildings, cadastral parcels, zoning plans, BGT and elevation, with a measuring tool.

siteplan.title: A site plan at true scale
siteplan.desc: Draw on a fixed A2 or A3 sheet with CPT markers, a CPT grid, dimension lines and RD coordinates, with a PDF or image as underlay and a title block. Then request quotes: the app sorts CPT contractors by distance to the project and prepares a request in your mail app.

calc.title: Calculations you can check
calc.desc: Work out the bearing capacity of piles, build a capacity table per CPT or calculate a laterally loaded pile. Every calculation sheet shows the formula, the filled-in values and the outcome next to the input. Bundle it all into a CPT report or a foundation advice report as a PDF.

formats.title: GEF and BRO-XML
formats.desc: CPTs as GEF 1.x or BRO-XML (CPT_O and CPT_O_DP) and boreholes from BHR-GT. Import messages stay with the project and can be exported as CSV or JSON.

chart.title: The CPT chart
chart.desc: qc, fs, Rf and u2 against depth in m NAP, with indicative qc/Rf soil zones. The zones are indicative, not a normalised classification.

borehole.title: Boreholes
borehole.desc: BRO boreholes with soil layers, admixtures and humus content, next to the CPTs in the same project.

compare.title: CPTs side by side
compare.desc: Put many CPTs side by side and scale the columns with the zoom, or fit them to the window.

bro.title: Load an area from the BRO
bro.desc: Fetch every CPT and borehole in the visible map area from the Dutch subsurface register (BRO).

layers.title: PDOK map layers
layers.desc: Background maps, aerial photos from 2016 to 2025, BAG buildings, cadastral parcels, zoning plans, BGT and elevation, with a measuring tool.

siteplan.title: Site plan
siteplan.desc: An A2 or A3 sheet at true scale with CPT markers, a CPT grid, dimension lines, RD tags, an underlay from PDF or an image, snapping to buildings and parcels, and a title block.

quotes.title: Request quotes
quotes.desc: The app sorts CPT contractors by distance to the project, preselects the three nearest and opens your mail app with a filled-in request. You adjust the choice before you send.

bearing.title: Bearing capacity of a pile
bearing.desc: Steel, concrete and timber piles, including timber with a concrete extension. The sheet shows the input and the CPT next to the worked-out result, with a print preview and PDF.

table.title: Capacity table
table.desc: Rc;net;d per CPT for a range of pile sizes and toe levels. Enter the capacity you need and see per size the shortest pile that reaches it and how much the toe level varies between CPTs.

lateral.title: Laterally loaded pile
lateral.desc: A beam on linear or non-linear soil springs, with the section and reinforcement as a drawing. Output: displacement, moment and shear, the soil reaction per layer, the N-M interaction and a PDF.

pileTable.title: Pile table
pileTable.desc: Many laterally loaded piles in one table, with per row its own head load, the utilisation ratio and the lightest standard size that passes.

settings.title: Settings per calculation
settings.desc: Pile factors from the table or as a project value, standard size series, subgrade values and pu profiles per soil type.

verified.title: Verified
verified.desc: The lateral pile kernel is compared with closed-form solutions and an independent solver; the bearing capacity with an external reference calculation and 100 public reference cases.

report.title: CPT report
report.desc: Cover, coordinate table, overview map and one page per CPT, in the OpenAEC house style.

advice.title: Foundation advice
advice.desc: One PDF with cover, table of contents, soil investigation, site plan, soil profile, pile advice and appendices. The texts per pile system are drafts for the consultant to check.

project.title: One project file
project.desc: A project is one .ifcgeo file (IFCX JSON) with the CPTs, the import messages, the site plan and the calculations. Older .ifcgis and .ifcx projects still open.

export.title: Open formats out
export.desc: Save as GEF, CSV or GeoJSON, or as an IFCX snapshot. You can open IFC4x3 to inspect it.

mcp.title: Works with an AI assistant
mcp.desc: An MCP server controls the open window on your own computer: open files, change project data and pile calculations, and write a PDF report.

languages.title: Ten languages
languages.desc: The interface is available in ten languages. The calculation modules and their reports are in Dutch only.

download.label: Download
download.title: Download v2026.45.8
download.lead: Free and without an account. Signed installers for Windows, macOS and Linux.
download.mobileNote: Open Geotechniek Studio is a desktop app for a large screen. Download it on your computer.
download.note: There is no built-in updater yet: install a new version over the old one. Your projects are ordinary files and stay where they are.

whatsnew.label: New in v2026.45.8
whatsnew.title: A pile table, a foundation advice report and its own logo
whatsnew.desc: Released on 6 November 2026. This version gives the app its approved logo. The release from the same day, v2026.45.7, brought the pile table for laterally loaded piles and the foundation advice report.

logo.title: Its own app logo
logo.desc: The approved logo is now in the app and in the installers and app icons.

pileTable.title: Pile table
pileTable.desc: One table for many laterally loaded piles with the same soil and section. Each row has its own head load, and a cell that fails turns red.

lightest.title: Lightest size
lightest.desc: For each pile, the lightest standard size that meets the utilisation ratio and the limit for head displacement, with a button to apply it.

advice.title: Foundation advice as a report
advice.desc: CPTs and pile calculations together in one PDF, with a cover, table of contents, a site plan to scale and appendices.

layer.title: Bearing layer
layer.desc: The advice shows an indicative bearing layer for each CPT; you set the limits for it yourself.

mcp.title: More for the AI assistant
mcp.desc: Through MCP an assistant can now also fill the pile table and add, change and export a foundation advice report as a PDF.

cost.a: Nothing. Open Geotechniek Studio is open source under the MIT licence: no licence fees, no account and no lock-in.

concept.q: Can I use the pile calculations directly?
concept.a: No. The calculations are concept: they show every step, but they do not replace a checked design. They carry a concept mark on screen and in every PDF. Have the results checked by a qualified consultant.

files.a: CPTs as GEF or BRO-XML, boreholes as BRO BHR-GT, projects as .ifcgeo, and older .ifcgis and .ifcx projects. You can also open IFCX and IFC4x3. And you can load CPTs and boreholes straight from the BRO on the map.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: Windows x64, macOS on Apple silicon and Intel, and Linux x64 as .deb, AppImage or Snap.

language.q: Is the app available in English?
language.a: The interface is available in ten languages, including English. The calculation modules and their reports are in Dutch only, because they are based on Dutch CPTs and standards.

update.q: How do I update to a new version?
update.a: There is no built-in updater yet. Download the new installer and install it over the old version. Your projects are ordinary files and stay where they are.

signed.a: Yes. Windows with Authenticode and a timestamp, macOS with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple, Linux with the OpenAEC OpenPGP key. The SHA256SUMS.txt file in every release lists the checksums of all files.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: The desktop app has an MCP server that controls the open window: open files, edit project data, add and change pile calculations, read the capacity table and write a PDF report. The server runs only on your own computer, and an indicator shows when an assistant is connected.

tech.heading: Technology
tech.sub: Open building blocks, also usable on their own.

tauri.title: Tauri 2
tauri.desc: Lightweight desktop apps for Windows, macOS and Linux.

ui.title: React and TypeScript
ui.desc: The interface, with the shared look, fonts and icons of the OpenAEC Blueprint.

rust.title: Rust crates
rust.desc: The CPT parsers, charts and reports come from the shared OpenAEC crates-warehouse.

core.title: Node core with HTTP API
core.desc: The same GEF and BRO parser also runs without a window, with an HTTP API and MCP.

sdk.title: Native SDK
sdk.desc: An SDK with a C interface for Windows and Linux, shipped with every release.

ifcx.title: IFCX
ifcx.desc: The project format is IFCX JSON: open and readable by anyone.

why.title: Why Open Geotechniek Studio?
why.desc: Free and open: no licence fees, no account and no lock-in. Open formats in and out, the BRO and PDOK right on the map, reports you can hand over and calculations you can check. For geotechnical consultants, structural engineers and everyone in civil engineering who works with CPTs.
